observations.statement: A finite benchmark can falsify a universal algorithmic claim but cannot establish a polynomial worst-case bound over all input lengths.
observations.support: This follows from the quantifier difference between finitely many tested inputs and a universal asymptotic statement.

observations.statement: A proposed polynomial representation is not a polynomial-time algorithm unless construction time, representation size, coefficient precision, evaluation time, and witness recovery are all polynomially bounded.
observations.support: Each omitted resource can encode exponential work or information.

observations.statement: Lower bounds for a direct encoding do not automatically refute a conjecture that permits polynomial-size auxiliary-variable lifts; the lower bound must quantify over the allowed lift class.
observations.support: The logical target of the lower bound must match the quantifiers of the registered hypothesis.

observations.statement: A hypothesis that merely asserts the existence of a polynomial-time SAT-deciding invariant without independently defining it is a restatement of P = NP, not progress toward it.
observations.support: The asserted invariant already is the missing polynomial-time decision procedure.

observations.statement: The Genesis survivors share one structural theme: they seek a polynomial-size exact lift into a mathematical class with an established polynomial-time decision algorithm.
observations.support: H001 uses bounded-treewidth dynamic programming, H002 submodular minimization, H003 linear programming over a totally unimodular system, and H004 constant-level semidefinite programming.
